original_note: title_bis "Bakal Core Magnetic Poles" uses bakal, which in Cebuano means TO BUY, not iron (puthaw). The card's own body uses the correct word — "natunaw nga puthaw sa outer core" — so the title is the outlier: the heading names a different thing (buying) than "Molten Iron Poles" and is never corrected within the title itself. This is the confirmed bakal false-friend pattern, in the title, with body evidence against it.
fact_en: Deep inside Earth, melted iron in the outer core keeps moving! This creates electric currents and a giant magnetic field, giving us our North and South magnetic poles.
fact_bis: Sa sulod sa Yuta, natunaw nga puthaw sa outer core naglihok! Naghimo kini og electric currents ug dako nga magnetic field, mao nga naa tay North ug South magnetic poles.

original_note: TAGALOG FALSE FRIEND IN TITLE. title_en "Plastic Never Rots" -> title_bis "Plastik nga Dili Mabulok". 'mabulok' is Tagalog for rot; in Cebuano 'bulok' is not rot (dull/colour sense), so the title does not deliver "does not rot" at all. The card's OWN body uses the correct Cebuano: "Ang plastik dili madunot sama sa dahon o pagkaon" — strongest evidence the title is the defect. Fix: "Plastik nga Dili Madunot".
fact_en: Plastic doesn't rot like leaves or food — it stays in the ocean for ages, so garbage patches keep growing as new trash piles up!
fact_bis: Ang plastik dili madunot sama sa dahon o pagkaon — magpabilin kini sa dagat sa dugay kaayo, busa padayon nga modako ang garbage patch samtang nagdugang ang basura!

original_note: title_bis "Dali Mabulok nga Kaon" for "Fast Food Spoilage". Bulok in Cebuano = COLOUR (the confirmed false friend; spoil/rot = madunot). The card's OWN body uses the correct word twice ("paspas madunot ang pagkain", "pagkadunot"), which marks the title as the outlier rather than regional variation. Title as shipped reads "quickly-coloured eating", not "food spoils fast".
fact_en:
Why does food spoil so fast in the Philippines?

The high humidity speeds up food spoilage and mold growth! That's why we should refrigerate food or store it in a dry place.
fact_bis:
Ngano paspas madunot ang pagkain sa Pilipinas?

Ang taas nga humidity nagpadasig sa pagkadunot sa pagkain ug pagtubo sa amag! Mao kini ang hinungdan kung ngano importante ang pag-refrigerate sa pagkain o pagtipig niini sa mamala nga lugar.

original_note: EN "Soft parts decay too quickly to become fossils" -> BIS "Paspas ra mabulok ang humok nga bahin". `bulok` = COLOUR in Cebuano (this corpus: "mabulokon nga bulak", "pinakabulokon nga balhibo", "mabulokon ang taklobo"); decay is `madunot`, used in 234 other cards. The causal clause that answers the card's own question is destroyed (reads "the soft part quickly becomes coloured"); the same sentence also uses Tagalog `matagas` for hard instead of `gahi`.
fact_en:
Why do fossils form more easily when an animal is quickly buried in sediment?

Because hard parts like bones and shells preserve much longer! Soft parts decay too quickly to become fossils.
fact_bis:
Nganong mas sayon maporma ang fossils kon paspas nga malubong ang hayop sa sediment?

Tungod kay mas dugay nagpabilin ang matagas nga bahin sama sa bukog ug shells! Paspas ra mabulok ang humok nga bahin.

original_note: The whole point of a binary cycle is that the secondary fluid BOILS at a low temperature. EN: "The isobutane boils easily and spins the turbine". BIS: "Sayon mosinaw ang isobutane ug mopalikid sa turbine" — sinaw is shine/shiny (corpus: masinaw nga dahon, sinaw nga perlas), never boil; the corpus renders "boil" as mobukal/nagbukal in 144 cards. No other sentence in the card says bukal or singaw, so the mechanism is gone: the child reads that isobutane "shines easily" and cannot say why a cooler geothermal fluid can still drive the turbine.
fact_en: Binary cycle geothermal plants heat a secondary fluid like isobutane using lower-temperature geothermal fluid! The isobutane boils easily and spins the turbine, even when the geothermal fluid isn't hot enough for direct flash steam.
fact_bis: Ang binary cycle geothermal plants nagpainit sa ikaduha nga likido sama sa isobutane gamit ang mas bugnaw nga geothermal fluid! Sayon mosinaw ang isobutane ug mopalikid sa turbine, bisan dili igo ang kainit alang sa direktang flash steam.

original_note: Body: "Ang inner core sa Yuta usa ka init ug solido nga bola nga kasagaran bakal ug nickel!" for "made mostly of iron and nickel". Cebuano *bakal* = TO BUY; iron is *puthaw* (the confirmed false friend). The fact-bearing sentence therefore never names the metal — a Cebuano-only child reads "a ball mostly buy and nickel". Evidence this is the defective field, not my ear: the card's OWN title_bis uses the correct word ("Inner Core Puthaw"), and the corpus uses *puthaw* for iron in the nutrition cards ("dato sa puthaw", "kalsiyum ug puthaw"). Partly mitigated by the title carrying *puthaw*, so ra
fact_en:
What is hiding deep inside Earth's center?

Earth's inner core is a hot, solid ball made mostly of iron and nickel!
fact_bis:
Unsa ang natago sa kinahiladman sa Yuta?

Ang inner core sa Yuta usa ka init ug solido nga bola nga kasagaran bakal ug nickel!

original_note: "Ang half-life mao ang panahon aron mabulok ang katunga sa radioactive isotope." Mabulok is the Tagalog word for rot/decay; in Cebuano bulok = COLOUR (also dull/stupid). Cebuano decay = madunot (used correctly in ffct-35415 "dali madunot"). The card's whole definition of half-life hangs on this verb and nothing restores it.
fact_en:
How do rocks tell time?

A half-life is the time for half a radioactive isotope to decay. Since this rate is constant, it acts as a natural clock to measure rock age!
fact_bis:
Unsaon pagsulti sa oras sa mga bato?

Ang half-life mao ang panahon aron mabulok ang katunga sa radioactive isotope. Tungod kay kanunay ang katulin niini, kini natural nga orasan sa pagsukod sa edad sa bato!

original_note: bis "Ang uling ug lana nagtipig og enerhiya..." for "Coal and oil store energy that plants captured from sunlight long ago". Cebuano `lana` = COCONUT OIL; petroleum/fossil oil is `langis` or `petrolyo` (the card's own terms list carries "langis"). The fossil-fuel fact is the whole card, and the Cebuano names an ordinary kitchen coconut oil instead — the child learns "charcoal and coconut oil are ancient stored sunlight", which is false of coconut oil and never corrected (the opening line only says "gasolina sa makina" generically). `uling` for coal is fine on its own; the defect is `lana`.
fact_en:
Did you know that the fuels in our engines actually began as solar energy?

Coal and oil store energy that plants captured from sunlight long ago, turning ancient sun into fuel!
fact_bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga ang mga gasolina sa makina nagsugod sa enerhiya sa Sun?

Ang uling ug lana nagtipig og enerhiya nga nakuha sa tanom gikan sa kahayag sa Sun kaniadto!

original_note: Title 'Opaque: Babag ug Bukal' and body 'gipabukal ang uban' use bukal (Cebuano: TO BOIL) for 'reflect'. The card's core fact is that opaque materials block, absorb AND reflect light, which is why you see their colour and shape; a child reading only the Cebuano gets 'made some of it boil' and never learns reflection. Nothing in the card restores it. Same batch uses the correct word: dcard-07322/dcard-07324 say 'motalbog' for light bouncing, and dcard-07415 uses bukal correctly for a boiling spring.
fact_en: Opaque materials block light, but they also absorb some of it and reflect some of it, which is why you can see their color and shape.
fact_bis: Gibabagan sa mga opaque nga materyales ang kahayag, apan gisuhop usab nila ang uban niana ug gipabukal ang uban, mao nga makita nimo ang ilang kolor ug porma.
